_comment: The texts of Crackdown's README that are its own (tools/title_readme.py has the common ones).

screens.alt: Pacific City, drawn by Any360's Vulkan renderer

pitch: It follows [saulob's PC port](https://github.com/saulob/crackdown-xbox360-recompiled) (currently v0.6.2: launcher, offline achievements, 4K and ultrawide, keyboard and mouse) and works on one goal: the game on its own code, with nothing of the console left under it, the Steam Deck as the first target and Windows running the same code.

state.recompiled: the whole game plays, as upstream's port does
state.library: five memory functions (`memcpy`, its forward copy, `memmove`, `memset`, the vector copy), compared with the game's own code on every call in game (21 M calls in the city for the first three)
state.game: the first functions rewritten and verified in a sandbox (the count is in the table above)

run: Both bindings are opt-in until they become the default:

`--any360_gpu=true` draws the game through `any360::gfx` (160-220 FPS at 1440p with 4x MSAA in the city on an RTX 5070 Ti); `--any360_sys_groups` puts the 248 system calls the game imports on `any360::sys`. The library functions run on `any360::xdk` by default (`--any360_xdk_natives=false` runs the game's own; `--any360_xdk_verify=true` runs both on every call and compares them). Left without a frame limit the title screen runs above 1,500 frames a second and does not take the Start button: `--crackdown_frame_rate=60` until that is fixed.
build: Windows, Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ and Clang tools: `tools\build.ps1` builds `build\crackdown.exe`, as upstream's port does ([docs/LEGACY_README.md](docs/LEGACY_README.md) has upstream's page: installing, the launcher, hotkeys, features, known issues). The build needs an [Any360](https://github.com/GaetanVigner/Any360) checkout next to this repository (`../any360`, or `-DCRACKDOWN_ANY360_DIR=<path>`).
fork: Besides Any360 under the game, this repository works on **a renderer that knows the game**: once the game's draws reach a renderer that understands them as passes and objects instead of Xbox 360 command packets, the same draw records feed FSR upscaling (motion vectors need per-object draw identity) and, later and optionally, ray-traced lighting. On the Steam Deck's four cores the emulation of the console's GPU, not the GPU itself, is the limit.
